EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman line at 2242 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a cyano (C≡N) stretching vibration, which is absent in most candidates but is present in molecule 10 (N#Cc1ccc(F)cc1). Molecule 10 also contains an aromatic ring, matching the strong ring C=C stretch at 1606 cm⁻¹ and the aromatic C–H stretch at 3089 cm⁻¹. The para-substituted benzene framework typically shows intense C–H out-of-plane bends near 820–850 cm⁻¹, accounting for the strong 840 cm⁻¹ band (and the weaker 818 cm⁻¹ shoulder). Fluoro-aryl compounds exhibit C–F stretches and bends in the 1100–1300 cm⁻¹ and 500–700 cm⁻¹ regions, consistent with the observed 1171, 1200, 1230 cm⁻¹ and the 548 cm⁻¹ and 649 cm⁻¹ peaks. No other candidate simultaneously provides a C≡N group, an aromatic ring, and a C–F bond to explain this full set of bands.
